title: Game of Life
summary: Conway’s Game of Life, printed in the terminal. You’ll store a grid in a Vec, read it from a picture, implement Display, and find patterns that repeat.

milestones.title: A grid
milestones.build: Store the cells in one `Vec<bool>`, row by row: cell (x, y) is at `y * width + x`. Fill in `new`, `width`, `height`, `get`, `set` and `population`. Anything outside the grid is dead.

milestones.title: Read a picture
milestones.build: `Grid::parse` reads rows of `#` and `.`. Every row must be as wide as the first; report the first problem as a `ParseError` with its line number.

milestones.title: Print it
milestones.build: Implement `Display` for `Grid` so `println!("{grid}")` and `to_string()` draw the same picture `parse` reads. `write!` and `writeln!` write into the formatter.

milestones.title: Neighbours
milestones.build: `live_neighbours` counts the live cells among the eight around a cell. Working in `isize` makes the `-1` offsets easy; skip anything outside the grid.

milestones.title: The next generation
milestones.build: `step` builds the next grid from the rules: two or three neighbours keep a cell alive, exactly three bring one to life. Read from `self` and write into a new grid.

milestones.title: Wrap around
milestones.build: `with_wrap(true)` turns the grid into a torus: a glider leaving on the right comes back on the left. `rem_euclid` wraps `-1` to the last column.

milestones.title: Oscillators
milestones.build: `period` steps forward until the grid matches where it started. A block has period 1, a blinker 2. Then watch it run: `cargo run`.
